newsitem.title: USA: Zimmerman sentenced for 1992 CBOT bond scheme.
newsitem.headline: Zimmerman sentenced for 1992 CBOT bond scheme.

text.p: Darrell Zimmerman, who pleaded guilty to two counts of wire fraud stemming from a 40-minute attempt to corner the U.S. Treasury bond futures market in 1992, was sentenced to 41 months in prison Tuesday.

U.S. District Judge William Hart also ordered Zimmerman to pay $10,000 in restitution to Lee B Stern & Co, the clearing firm that lost $8 million from the trading spree by Zimmerman and his accomplice, Anthony Catalfo.
"I have to take account of the enormous loss that was incurred," Hart said in his ruling.

On October 22, 1992, Zimmerman and Catalfo entered orders in the bond futures and options pits at the Chicago Board of Trade, even though neither of the amateur traders had the capital to cover those positions, according to court documents.
Zimmerman and Catalfo told floor brokers they were managing large sums of money for outside investors.

Lee Stern, who now heads LBS LTD Partnership, a non-clearing firm, said in an interview after the sentencing, "My only regret is the floor brokers who knowingly accepted orders that were so outrageous."
Lee B Stern & Co, which had been clearing futures trades for about 25 years, closed down after the 1992 bond incident.
Zimmerman pleaded for leniency at Tuesday's sentencing, arguing that he voluntarily pleaded guilty in September to two counts of wire fraud.
Zimmerman fled to his native Vancouver, British Columbia, after he and Catalfo were indicted on six counts of wire fraud in 1993. He was extradited to the United States in July 1996.
According to assistant U.S. attorney James Conway, Zimmerman will be deported from the U.S. after he completes his sentence.
In addition, Zimmerman will be under supervisory probation for three years following his prison sentence.

Catalfo, who was found guilty of six counts of mail and wire fraud by a jury in 1994, will complete his sentence in May, Conway said. Hart sentenced Catalfo to 3-1/2 years in prison. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
